desc: THE anchor source for this lane. Pooled Ionis integrated safety database: 59 trials, 16 distinct 2'-MOE PS ASOs, 3,476 subjects. Verified full text via efetch (132 KB XML) AND the 10-page supplementary PDF via the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles zip endpoint (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC5467133/supplementaryFiles) - all tables text-extractable. Table 1: 16 ASOs with ISIS number, target gene, full 5'->3' sequence, gapmer design (5-10-5 etc.), trial and subject counts - populates oligos.csv directly. Table 2: dose ranges (mg/week) and treatment duration by indication. Table 3: incidence of confirmed platelet reductions, phase 1-3, panel A (normal-baseline subjects) and panel B, cross-tabulated by 5 platelet-count bands (LLN-100, <100-75, <75-50, <50-25, <25 K/uL) and 2 relative bands (<0.7xBSLN, <0.5xBSLN) against placebo, ASO total, and SIX dose bands (>0-75, >75-175, >175-275, >275-375, >375-475, >475 mg/week) - this table alone is the dose-response backbone. Table 4: mipomersen-specific confirmed post-baseline platelet reductions, total/6-month/1-year phase 3 RCTs vs placebo. Table 5: proportion of ASOs with >10% incidence of >30% platelet decline, by dose band. Table 6: platelet reductions stratified by antithrombotic co-medication use. Table 7: bleeding-event incidence, mipomersen vs placebo. Fig 1: platelet level over time (percent change and absolute count) for ISIS 104838 in a 12-week phase 2 RA trial. Supplementary Tables S4 (DDI trials), S6 (42 randomized placebo-controlled trials, full dose x threshold grid), S7 (on- vs post-treatment), S8 (subject-level meta-analysis of mean % change by dose), S9 (subject-level meta-analysis of incidence), S11 (bleeding events), S12 (coagulation-time abnormalities).

desc: Verified: HTTP 200, 121 pages, 49 pages containing platelet content, parsed with PyMuPDF. The definitive public-domain record of volanesorsen's dose-limiting thrombocytopenia, and it supersedes the paywalled APPROACH (NEJM) and COMPASS (Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol) primary papers. Table 37 (p91): 'Summary of Confirmed Nadir Post-Baseline Platelet Counts in Study CS6 (APPROACH)' - full 5-band nadir distribution (100-140k, 75-100k, 50-75k, 25-50k, 0-25k per mm3) for placebo n=33 vs volanesorsen n=33, plus <140,000 and <100,000 cumulative rows (24/33 = 75.0% vs 8/33 = 24.2%; <100,000 in 15/32 = 46.9% vs 0%). Table 38 (p92): same for Study CS16 (COMPASS), N=113 - NOTE this one is an embedded image, needs vision extraction. Table 39 (p94): fully text-extractable - dose, average baseline platelet count, average nadir platelet count and average nadir % change from baseline, split by body weight <70 kg (N=11, nadir 76 x10^9/L, -62.3%) vs >=70 kg (N=8, nadir 126 x10^9/L, -43.3%). Table 40 (p98): per-patient listing of every platelet decrease to <50,000/mm3 across CS2, CS6 and CS16 with preferred term, platelet nadir, time to onset, duration, associated bleeding events and discontinuation action. Table 41 (p99): per-patient nadir count, initial monitoring frequency, dose regimen at onset, time to decline from >100,000 to nadir (days), time to recover to >50,000 and to >140,000 - text-extractable, spans CS2/CS6/CS16/CS7. Table 22 (p60): actions taken in patients with low platelet count in CS6. Figure 20: platelet decline time course reaching a plateau ~30% below baseline. Narrative (p90-92) adds CS6 mean nadir 134,000/mm3 at Week 25 vs 207,000 placebo, mean change -48,000 vs +25,000, AE incidences (platelet count decreased 30% vs 3%; thrombocytopenia 12% vs 0% in CS6; 4% vs 5% and 13% vs 5% in CS16), 2 grade-4 (<25,000/mm3) events leading to discontinuation, and CS7 open-label figures (platelet count decreased 18%, thrombocytopenia 9%).
title: Waylivra (volanesorsen) EPAR Public Assessment Report

desc: Verified: HTTP 200, 10.2 MB, 223 pages, 64 pages with platelet content (IMPORTANT: accessdata.fda.gov returns 404 to a default curl UA - a browser User-Agent is required). Contains Evelyn Mentari's full Clinical Safety Review section 8.5 'Thrombocytopenia' with the most granular public inotersen platelet data anywhere. Table 24 (p140): subjects with decreased platelet measurements, central and local lab values, Studies CS2 and CS3 (image - vision extraction). Table 25 (p141): the explicit bimodal typology - 'Rare' (rapid onset, severe, catastrophic fatal bleeding) vs 'Common' (gradual slow decline, often mild) - text-extractable and maps directly onto the schema's grade-3 vs grade-1 split. Table 31 (p154): antiplatelet antibody test results cross-tabulated against platelet-count change, Study CS2. Table 32 (p155): subjects with nadir platelet count <75 x10^9/L AND treatment-emergent positive antiplatelet antibodies. Table 33 (p159): post-baseline nadir platelets and dose exposure by baseline platelet count. Table 34 (p160): FULLY TEXT-EXTRACTABLE - frequency and relative risk of nadir <75 x10^9/L by baseline platelet count: CS2 10/39 (25.6%) for baseline <200 x10^9/L vs 3/73 (4.1%) for >=200, RR 6.2; longitudinal CS2+CS3 15/39 (38.5%) vs 4/73 (5.5%), RR 7.0. Narrative p141 gives CS2 <100 x10^9/L in 28/112 (25.0%) inotersen vs 1/60 (1.7%) placebo; <75 x10^9/L in 16/112 (14.3%) vs 0/60; <25 x10^9/L (severe) in 3 (2.7%); 71% of subjects had a >=30% post-treatment platelet decline. Individual clinical summaries follow for all 3 severe-thrombocytopenia subjects including the fatal intracranial haemorrhage. The companion OtherR.pdf (232 pp, 5.6 MB, same URL pattern) is a Division of Hematology Products consult with its own Tables 2-7 and 14-17 restating the sponsor's Summary of Clinical Safety tables 64/67/69 - overlapping but independently citable (e.g. its narrative gives <100 x10^9/L as 26/112 = 23.2% vs 1/60 = 1.6%, and a 22.4% incidence-rate difference, 95% CI 13.9-31.0).

desc: Verified: HTTP 200, 142 pages, 42 pages with platelet content, PyMuPDF text-extractable. desc: VERIFIED: the PMC/efetch record is ABSTRACT-ONLY (10 kB, no <body>) and the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint returns nothing, but the Europe PMC PDF-render URL above returns HTTP 200 with a real 1,218,316-byte 10-page PDF that parses to 51,319 characters of full text via PyMuPDF — this is the route that works, do not use efetch for this one. The best APTAMER-modality source in the lane, and the only one covering the PF4/HIT-like idiosyncratic axis with human platelets. Four aptamers of different length and secondary structure (15mer-DNA thrombin aptamer, 44mer-DNA activated-protein-C aptamer, 57mer-RNA tetracycline aptamer, 77mer-RNA FMN aptamer) plus a construct series (10mer-ssDNA, 21mer-hairpin RNA, 21mer-dsDNA and two other 21mer DNA secondary structures, 45mer double-stem-loop RNA I and II, the sequence-matched 45mer double-stem-loop DNA, 45mer-polyA, 45mer-polyC, single nucleotides, cellular RNA +/- RNase A). Fig 5D EIA optical densities of human anti-PF4/heparin IgG against PF4/aptamer complexes (PF4/heparin control OD 1.130+/-0.143; 44mer aptamer 1.098+/-0.140 over 5-30 ug/mL; 15mer aptamer only 0.431+/-0.064 at 40 ug/mL; reduced to 0.593+/-0.203 by 660 ug/mL heparin, P<.0001) plus a functional heparin-induced-platelet-activation assay with human HIT sera. Sequences and mfold secondary structures for every construct are in Fig 1. desc: Verified full text via efetch (177 KB XML, license cc by-nc). The lane's NEGATIVE-CONTROL source and the direct chemistry contrast to the unconjugated gapmers in Crooke 2017 - GalNAc conjugation cuts the dose ~10-20x and the platelet signal disappears entirely. desc: 271 pp, 52 platelet hits. High scientific value as a SPECIES-TRANSLATION CONTRAST: the human Kynamro label contains zero platelet/thrombocytopenia/bleeding content (verified), yet the 1-year cynomolgus monkey study at 30 mg/kg/week (~10x clinical exposure) produced thrombocytopenia in 3 high-dose monkeys requiring dosing holidays of various durations, with platelet counts recovering on drug withdrawal in 2 of 3. Per-animal detail: HD female #5506 sacrificed moribund on Day 271 (Week 39) while on a platelet-driven dosing holiday (last dose Day 239), with a 30-minute post-venipuncture bleed, widespread multifocal hemorrhage at postmortem; animals #5007 and #5506 had the greatest platelet reductions AND the greatest up-regulation of the platelet activation marker CD62P, alongside decreased plasma C3 (complement consumption) — the review proposes complement-mediated platelet activation, increased consumption and splenic removal, with splenomegaly and platelet sequestration; #5505 and #5506 showed macrophage/histiocyte extravascular destruction of RBCs and/or platelets (HLH-like). Also contains a lifetime mouse study and a named mouse surrogate oligo, ISIS 147764, usable as an additional compound. Same 2'-MOE full-PS gapmer chemistry class as inotersen — a within-chemistry comparator.
title: FDA Pharmacology/Toxicology Review, NDA 203568 Kynamro (mipomersen), R. Wange Ph.D.
